All 19 references in ffe.asm are reads, 17 of them full dwords (`mov eax,[DATA_008958]' / `push dword [DATA_008958]'), and FUNC_000855 copies it into the generator's record at rec+0xc (ffe.asm:59903-59904). This is `resb' space, so nothing is stored there statically and there is no x86 byte order to preserve; `plain' is what the 17 dword sites need and it costs nothing anywhere else. WHY NOT be32 (tried, measured, rejected): it needs a 4-byte group, so DATA_008958 must absorb DATA_008959's byte, and bumping its size desynchronises storage.resolve's forward walk -- three functions reaching [DATA_008804+16204] through that walk began refusing with "not one aligned big-endian group". KNOWN AND DELIBERATE with `plain': that byte read still lands on the id's LOW byte where x86 means its TOP byte, and `mov ax,[DATA_008958]' (58572) still reads the wrong half -- both exactly as wrong as they were before this entry, both on the system-information screen rather than the generation path, and both needing symbolic sub-word displacement machinery that does not exist yet.

label: DATA_005103
evidence: THE CONSOLE BUTTON ARRAY, records 1..81. Four labels are views into one 82 x 62-byte record array (ffe.asm:20336 walks it with `add ebx,byte +0x3e`, 0x52 iterations). DATA_005101 already carries `byte-only+le` for exactly this reason; DATA_005103 was missed and the manifest stores it `plain` -- because ConsoleSetButtonImage takes its ADDRESS (`mov eax,DATA_005103`, ffe.asm:20391), and convert_static's raw fallback records an address-taken label as 'plain' (no swap) instead of 'le' (raw + swap at every named access). The consequence: `mov eax,[eax*2+DATA_005102]` (curindex) and `mov ecx,[eax*2+DATA_005103]` (radio id) at 20384-20385, and the WRITE at 20407, all read x86-ordered dwords. Record 0's copies live in DATA_005102, which IS 'le' and therefore correct -- so button 0 works and the other 81 do not. FUNC_000261_ConsoleDrawButtons then uses curindex as a SCALED index (`lea eax,[ebx+eax*4-0x30]`), so a curindex of 1 stored the wrong way round reads 0x01000000 and addresses 64 MB past the array: blank captions, and a hard machine reset when F3 makes ConsoleSetButtonImage write a fresh curindex. The size is not a multiple of 4 (5026) and the record stride is 62, so no dword grouping of the label can ever be right -- raw storage with the swap in the emitted code is the only correct form, and lower.py already carries it for both loads (lower.py:856) and stores (lower.py:886).

label: DATA_009128
evidence: THE VIEW OBJECT'S MODEL-NUMBER FIELD, and the first realisation of the residual risk storage.py's own 'plain' docstring names: 'a mixed-width field shared between a pointer and a name'. DATA_009127 (resb 130) and DATA_009128 (resb 26) are ONE runtime object record split across two labels; offset 0x82 of that record IS DATA_009128+0. The record's base address is taken (mov ebx,DATA_009127 ffe.asm:71524, push dword DATA_009127 71642) so DATA_009127 classifies 'plain', but DATA_009128's ONLY reference in the whole disassembly is a NAMED dword store, mov [DATA_009128],eax at ffe.asm:71640, and convert_static.py:280 gives 'plain' only to address-taken labels, so it fell to 'le'. The translator then SWAPS that store -- build\xlat-full\FUNC_000960.s emits move.l d0,d7 / rol.w #8,d7 / swap d7 under the comment "stored in x86 order ('le' in the storage manifest)" -- while every reader of the same field goes through a REGISTER base (FUNC_001682's mov eax,[ebx+0x82], ffe.asm:102206) and gets no correction. Written 176, read back 0xB0000000. MEASURED 2026-08-05 on both machines: 266 of our 510 model requests (52%) fell outside DATA_004681's range against 0 of the reference's 459, ALL 266 from a single return address resolving to FUNC_001682+0x1A, values exactly 0xB0000000 x155 and 0xB1000000 x111 -- 176 and 177 shifted into the top byte. FUNC_001538 then indexes mov eax,[eax*4+DATA_004681] with that and reads garbage, which is why the model interpreter resolved 1 vertex where the reference resolved 2705. MUST be byte-only+ptr and NOT dword-only+ptr: the label is 26 bytes, and _close_label's size%4 guard (convert_static.py:190) downgrades a be32 label that is not a whole number of dword groups straight back to 'le' -- dword-only+ptr was tried first and changed nothing.
